leading_positions.synthesis: Optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) appear in four of the eight round-1 configurations, two as the sole part (Kroll, Lindroth) and two as one part of a two-part prize (Danielsson, Pearce). All four name the same two laureates, and Johansson, Mehlig and Olsson list B043 as an alternative. What is shared is the clean two-name attribution, independent confirmation in Sr, Yb and Hg, and the view that the lattice step is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. What is not shared is whether the achievement counts as a discovery or as an advance in measurement. Kroll and Lindroth frame it as a measurement breakthrough; Danielsson and Pearce pair it with a discovery-type achievement because they doubt it suffices alone; Mehlig, Johansson and Olsson ask what new physics it teaches.

Two members propose a two-part prize pairing optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) with IceCube high-energy neutrino astronomy credited to Francis Halzen alone, keeping the union at three people. They agree on the pairing and on the single-name IceCube credit, and both rank the discovery of the diffuse flux and later source associations as a new observational window. They also concede that a lone name for a collaboration of hundreds is the weak point and that Karle and Yoshida have claims; Danielsson would drop the IceCube half rather than invent an artificial trio. Other members who addressed B010 (Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig, Olsson) accept it as a real discovery but say the attribution is unresolved, and none of them includes it in a configuration.

Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) is the single-part first choice of two members, with a theory-then-experiment structure and a new platform of correlated phases. Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce list it as an alternative. Supporters and sceptics agree the field is about eight years old, the pairing mechanism is unsettled, and credit overlaps with Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, Cao, Fatemi and Dean. They differ on whether a citation naming the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated states, not the mechanism, is mature enough now.

Circuit quantum electrodynamics is proposed by one member alone, with Girvin, Schoelkopf and Wallraff as the three names. Johansson holds it with reduced confidence and names B043 as the first alternative. Four credited names cannot be cut to three without omitting Blais or Girvin, and several members (Danielsson, Lindroth, Pearce) raise the 2025 superconducting-circuit prize as a timing problem.

Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp) are the first choice of one member, who now ranks fluctuation theorems below it. Eriksson, Olsson and Pearce keep B008 as an alternative or rank it near the top. All agree it is mature and well confirmed. They differ on the fourth credited name (Hasan versus Mele, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang uncredited) and on how much the 2016 topological-phases prize overlaps.

areas_of_agreement: Seven members place B043 in their preferred configuration or among their alternatives, and no member argues that the optical lattice clock is poorly confirmed or scientifically unsound; its independent confirmation across Sr, Yb and Hg is not disputed.

Danielsson, Lindroth and Pearce explicitly treat the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits as a timing obstacle for circuit QED, even though Johansson disputes that the two achievements overlap.
Members who comment on B010 accept that the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux is a genuine discovery; the objections concern credit, not the physics.

Several members want any citation to name specific demonstrated results (the 1e-18 performance for B043, the flat bands and correlated states for B029) and not an unsettled mechanism or a future event such as the redefinition of the second.
scientific_disputes: Whether the optical lattice clock is a discovery or an advance in measurement, and whether its physics yield so far (tests of constants, relativistic geodesy, many-body clock physics) is more than a refinement of the frequency-standard programme honoured in 2005 and 2012 (Mehlig, Johansson, Olsson against Kroll, Lindroth, Danielsson, Pearce).

Whether IceCube source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane), which rest on moderate statistical significance, strengthen the case for B010 beyond the diffuse flux (questions from Olsson and Johansson).

Whether the unresolved origin of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene leaves enough settled physics for a citation limited to flat bands and correlated insulating and superconducting phenomenology.
Whether a method-type theoretical framework such as DMFT (B019, Eriksson, now an alternative) counts as a discovery; Eriksson has stepped back from advocating it.
Whether a single coherent achievement or a two-part prize pairing unrelated fields is preferable.
attribution_disputes: IceCube (B010): Halzen alone, Halzen, Karle and Yoshida, or no naming at all, given a collaboration of hundreds and the AMANDA, Baikal and ANTARES precursors; Kroll cannot see a three-name subset the collaboration would accept, and Danielsson and Pearce disagree on how much Karle's detector and analysis leadership can be separated from Halzen's.

Optical lattice clocks (B043): whether Katori and Ye alone is defensible given contributions from Paris, Braunschweig, Lemonde, Pfau and the broader Boulder group, versus the view of Kroll and Lindroth that the two names map onto the concept and the record accuracy.
Twisted bilayer graphene (B029): whether Cao, Fatemi and Dean's group, and the earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto theory, should weigh against the credited trio.
Topological insulators (B008): Mele versus Hasan as the third theory or experiment name, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, Fu and Moore also uncredited.
Circuit QED (B023): Girvin versus Blais in a three-name cut.

Gamma-ray burst afterglows (B033): Costa, Frontera and Kulkarni with van Paradijs deceased and Piro, Djorgovski, Metzger and Frail also having claims; Danielsson and Pearce ranked it highly but neither includes it in a configuration.
maturity_disputes: Twisted bilayer graphene is about eight years old with an unsettled pairing mechanism; Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig see it as premature, while Kroll and Lindroth see it as less mature than the clock or as the natural next candidate, while Eriksson and Olsson regard the reproduced phenomenology as sufficient.

Whether the pending redefinition of the second should delay a lattice-clock prize; Kroll, Lindroth and Pearce's position as discussed is that the prize rewards demonstrated performance, but Olsson and Mehlig note that no deviation from existing theory has been seen and the main consequence has not occurred.
Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize reduces the standing of B008 as a separate principle (Mehlig and Olsson raise the question).
Whether circuit QED is premature or redundant following the 2025 circuit prize, against its two decades of confirmation.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (WACQT director, Chalmers) discloses proximity to the circuit QED community and says he should be treated as potentially conflicted on B023.

Kroll discloses a doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder and notes that Ye is associated with the JILA environment around Hall; he documents no tie to Katori or Ye and leaves it to the chair to judge. He also notes field proximity to B023.

Olsson flags long-standing exchanges with Japanese universities and a University of Tokyo fellowship as possibly relevant to Katori (B043), with no documented collaboration; she also notes that Johansson is a Chalmers colleague, though no shortlisted ballot credits a Chalmers person.
Eriksson discloses field proximity to DMFT (B019) and would consider recusing from a DMFT-centred part.

Pearce (chair) discloses that astroparticle and gamma-ray instrumentation is close to his own field (B010, B033) and that he supports B043 and B010 in his own configuration; no tie to a named candidate and no recusal requirement is apparent.
Lindroth, as an atomic physicist, notes that her views on B043, B006 and B027 may be tied to her field, with no conflict apparent for B043; Danielsson and Mehlig report no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B010: can any member identify a decisive individual contribution that separates Halzen from Karle and Yoshida, and is a one-name IceCube credit defensible in a prize whose other part has two laureates, or should the IceCube half be dropped if no clean credit exists?

For B043: do members who ranked the clock lower (Mehlig, Johansson, Olsson, Danielsson) accept the magic-wavelength lattice concept plus the 1e-18 demonstration as distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and is it sufficient alone or does it need a partner part?

For the three-person cap: does the committee prefer one coherent achievement (B043 alone, B029 or B008) or a two-part prize that pairs B043 with a second achievement, and what is the second part's best attribution?

For B029: if the citation names the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated insulating and superconducting states and not the mechanism, would Danielsson, Johansson and Mehlig regard it as mature enough this year, and how are Cao, Fatemi and the earlier Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto theory to be handled?

For B023 and B008: does the 2025 circuit prize rule out circuit QED, and does the 2016 topological-phases prize leave a separate Z2 and quantum spin Hall principle, and in either case is the Mele or Girvin question resolvable within three names?

For B033: can any member propose an attribution for gamma-ray burst afterglows that handles van Paradijs, Piro, Djorgovski, Metzger and Frail, or is the candidate effectively unavailable under the cap?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows partial convergence on B043 (explicit in four configurations, an alternative for three more) and a split on what to pair it with. IceCube (B010) has two explicit supporters, with attribution as the stated obstacle for everyone else. B029, B008 and B023 each have one or two single-part supporters, and each member's account of the main obstacle is attribution or timing and not the quality of the science. The supporters of B043 differ on whether it should stand alone or with a partner, and that question, together with the IceCube credit, is the main item for round 2.
